Accept this garland of flowers, giver of good fortune, health and prosperity; accept this incense, god, and make my devotion unshaking.
agnipuran:206:11	Give me the boon I desire and a good state hereafter, O best of sages, giver of the fruit of all desires, by gods and demons.

This arghya has been given by me with cloth, rice, fruits and gold; I shall awaken Agastya, what was raised by my mind;
agnipuran:206:13	I shall give arghya with fruits; accept the arghya, great sage. "Agastya, thus digging with spades, desiring offspring, progeny and strength, the fiery-splendored sage nourished both ears; true, he came to the blessings among the gods."
Princess, homage to you, wife of the sage, of great vows; accept the arghya, goddess of gods, Lopamudra, glorious.
A vessel furnished with five jewels, with gold and silver, covered with seven grains, joined with curd and sandal,
one should give as arghya to Agastya; for women and Shudras it is non-Vedic: "Agastya, tiger among sages, mass of splendor and giver of all,
having accepted this worship done by me, go for peace." One should give up one grain, one fruit, one juice in Agastya's name;
then one should feed Brahmins with food, ghee, pudding and sweets; a cow, garments and gold, and a fee one should give them.
With a vessel containing ghee and pudding covering its mouth, with gold, one should arrange that pot for a Brahmin.
Having given arghya for seven years, all obtain everything: water, sons, good fortune, a husband for the maiden, a royal-born one.
Honey-mixture, water for rinsing, bath, garment and scent, flower, incense, lamp and food offering and the rest — homage to you.
Thus in worship, vow and gift, hear the formula of gift together: "Today to the Brahmin of such gotra, Sharman by name,
this material, Vishnu its deity, for quieting all sins, for increase of life, health, good fortune and the rest,
for increase of the line, for victory and wealth, for dharma, lordship and desire, and for pacification of that sin,
for release from samsara I give this gift to you; for establishing this gift I give this to you;
by this may the lord of all worlds be pleased always. Lord of sacrifice, gift and vow, give me learning, fame and the rest;
give me dharma, desire, wealth and liberation, what my mind desires." One who daily reads or hears this compendium of vows and gifts
obtains his desires, stainless, and gains enjoyment and liberation. The vows of tithi, weekday, star, sankranti, yoga, Manvantara and the rest
are not in one way, by rule from Vasudeva and others, by worship.
The Shadashiti-mukhas (the eighty-six) are said to be eighty-six times in fruit. The past and future merits are the two solstices, northern and southern.
In Cancer thirty nadis, in Capricorn twenty are remembered; at the present Libra and Aries, ten nadis on both sides;
when the eighty-six has passed, sixty nadis are stated; called holy; at Vishnupadi sixteen before and after.
When in Shravana, Ashvini, Dhanishtha, with a serpent deity at the head, it falls on Sunday, it is called Vyatipata.
On the ninth of the bright half of Kartika the Krita (age) came out; Treta on the bright third of Vaishakha; the Dvapara age;
on the new moon of Magha, on the thirteenth in Nabhasya (Bhadrapada) of the dark half, one should know Kali; the Manvantara starts should be known.
The bright ninth of Ashvina and the twelfth of Kartika, the third of Magha and that of Bhadrapada,
the new moon of Phalguna, the eleventh of Pausha, the tenth of Ashadha, the seventh of Magha,
the dark eighth of Shravana, and the full moon of Ashadha, of Kartika and Phalguna likewise, and the fifteenth of Jyeshtha;
and above, the three Ashtakas of Agrahayani are declared; the eighth called Ashtaka; gifts in these are imperishable.
At Gaya, Ganga, Prayaga and the like, at a holy place, in temples and the like; unasked gifts, for learning; not a maiden.
One should give facing east and receive facing north; the giver's life increases, and the receiver's does not diminish.
Having pronounced the name and gotra of the recipient and of oneself, they give what is to be given; in the gift of a maiden, the three again.
Having bathed and worshipped, with the vyahritis one should give the gift with water: gold, horse, sesame, elephants, maidservants, chariot, land, house,
maiden and tawny cow — these are the ten great gifts. What is obtained through learning, valor, austerity, a daughter, officiating, or a pupil,
the bride-price, wealth, all of it, by following crafts; what is gained by moneylending, farming, trade, or by obligation,
by dice, gambling, theft, counterfeiting and rash acts, by deceit — all is of three kinds, with three kinds of fruit.
Woman's property is remembered as sixfold: gift before fire, gift at the bridal procession, given in love, received from brother, mother and father.
The property of Brahmin, Kshatriya and Vaishya, and of the Shudra by their favor; a cow, house, bed and women should not be given to many.
One who does not give what was promised destroys a hundred families; of the gods, teachers, and mother and father likewise,
merit should be given with effort, whatever merit is acquired anywhere. Wealth given with a desire for return is fruitless.
Dharma is accomplished by faith; even water given is imperishable. One endowed with knowledge, conduct and virtues, free of harming others,
by protecting and saving the ignorant, is remembered as the best recipient. A gift to the mother is a hundredfold; to the father a thousandfold is said;
to a daughter infinite; to a uterine brother imperishable. To a non-human the gift is equal; in a sinner it should be known to be of great fruit;
to one of mixed caste double; to a Shudra four times; to a Vaishya eightfold; to a Kshatriya sixteenfold; to one only nominally a Brahmin.
To a Vedic student a hundredfold; to a Veda teacher endless; to a priest, an officiant and the like the gift is called imperishable.
What is given to the destitute is endless, and to a sacrificer. A Brahmin without austerity and study, fond of accepting gifts,
sinks in water with that very gift as with a stone raft. Having bathed and rinsed well, one should accept, restrained and pure.
The receiver should always recite the Savitri; then he should recite along with the material the deity;
the receiver should recite aloud having received from a best Brahmin; softly from a Kshatriya; in a whisper from a Vaishya;
mentally from a Shudra; and the svasti recital. Fearlessness is of all deities; the earth has Vishnu as deity;
a maiden, a slave and a female slave are called Prajapati's; the elephant is called Prajapati's; the horse is Yama's;
and all one-hoofed, and the buffalo is Yama's; the camel is Nirriti's; the cow is Rudra's; the goat is Agni's;
the sheep is Water's; the boar is Hari's; wild animals are Vayu's; a reservoir is Varuna's, as are water-pots and the like;
sea-born jewels, gold and iron are Agni's; grains are Prajapati's, and cooked food too, best one;
scent they call Gandharva's; cloth is remembered as Brihaspati's; all birds are Vayu's; learning and the body are Brahma's;
books and the like are Sarasvati's; Vishvakarma has crafts; Vanaspati of trees and the like; the material deities are Hari's body.
Umbrella, black antelope skin, bed, chariot, seat, sandals and vehicle are said to be Uttanangira's;
war equipment, weapons, banner and the rest are of all deities; the house too is of all deities; of all, Vishnu is deity,
or Shiva, since there is no substance apart from him. One should take the name of the substance and say "I give";
then one should give water in the hand; this is remembered as the rule in gifts. "Vishnu is the giver, Vishnu the substance" — the receiver should say "I accept."
Svasti — receiving, dharma, enjoyment and liberation the two fruits. One who does not wish to rob teachers and dependents, intending to worship gods and ancestors,
may receive from everyone but should not be satisfied himself thereby. A Shudra's wealth is not for sacrifice; its fruit is the Shudra's.
Jaggery, buttermilk, juices and the like may be taken from a Shudra by one who has retired. A twice-born pressed by lack of livelihood may receive from everyone;
no fault accrues to Brahmins from teaching, officiating, or censured receiving; for they are like fire and sun.
In the Krita age it is given by going; in Treta it is given by bringing; in Dvapara to one who asks; in Kali with attendance.
Having intended the recipient in mind, one should pour water on the ground. The ocean has an end; there is no end to gift.

Today at an eclipse of sun or moon, Sankranti and the like, in time, at a holy place such as Ganga, Gaya, Prayaga, a land of great merit,
agnipuran:209:58	and to one of such gotra, Sharman by name, a great-souled recipient endowed with Veda and Vedangas,
agnipuran:209:59	this great material, by name so-and-so, with Vishnu and Rudra and others as deity, for sons, grandsons, house, lordship, wife, dharma, wealth, good qualities,
agnipuran:209:60	for increase of fame, learning, great desires, good fortune and health, for pacification of all sins, for heaven, for enjoyment and liberation,
agnipuran:209:61	I give this to you; may Hari and Shiva be pleased with me; destroyer of floods of divine, aerial and earthly portents,
agnipuran:209:62	for attaining dharma, wealth, desire and liberation, may it grant me the Brahma world. To the Brahmin of such name and gotra, Sharman,
agnipuran:209:63	for establishing this gift I give gold as fee. With this gift formula one should give all gifts.
With a thousand drona of grain is the best; the next are by halves; the best should be sixteen drona; the salt mountain.
